why: In next/, wrote the laws of docs/plan/quests/l10-boot-drain-PLAN.md in next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/dev/watch.laws.integration.test.ts, on the plan's yes to open question 1. L10 (renamed as the plan says) accounts for every install as the one owed change or an unchanged repeat in its own program's watch.rebuild span, gives each owed change its own 3 s bound, settles on a count of delivered Rolldown ENDs against ended rebuilds, never on quiet, and checks that started rebuilds never outnumber delivered ENDs and that the watchers reporting a change for a saved file number the programs that reach it (L10a to L10c). A new scenario law makes the four repeat orders on purpose (L10d and S1). fixtureValue gains values and saveWalk pins the shared element. The before-repair read matched the plan: change ids are absolute paths under the fixture home, one per reaching watcher per save, and none for shared/unused.ts. The laws are green on the unchanged product; their red is the old L10 assertions, which fail cases 1 to 3 of the scenario with run 2's shape and the old only-they-install line. L10 at full depth takes about 40 s, against 260 s before. No product file was touched.

The root is outside the plan: finding 2026-11-18-watch-laws-closed-builds-stay-reachable. pnpm lint ran once on an earlier draft (18 parts passed, lint:promise-types 0 findings) before the owner's rule change; after it only pnpm format and the leak grep ran.
